title: Mastering Data Visualization
summary: This reel provides a masterclass in data visualization, covering essential rules for honesty and clarity. It teaches viewers how to avoid misleading axes, choose the right chart types, use color meaningfully, and optimize the data-ink ratio.

transcript.text: This chart screams 400%, it's 4. This chart is lying.
The axis never started at zero. Truncate the baseline and a 2% gap looks like a cliff.
Bar charts start at zero. No exceptions.
Bars compare values side-by-side. Lines show change over time. Pie charts break the moment you pass five slices. Your eye can't rank angles.
Color isn't decoration, it's encoding. Categorical for groups, sequential for scale, diverging for above and below. One accent for the point. The rest goes gray.
Heavy gridlines, 3D bars, drop shadows—all noise. Tufte called it the data-ink ratio. Every pixel should be data. Label the line directly, drop the legend.
Same numbers. Squish the chart flat and the trend dies. Stretch it tall and it spikes. Aim for slopes near 45 degrees. That's where your eye reads change best.
Follow for more UI design. Save this for your next dashboard.
